function: Unsupervised heterogeneous GNN for joint uplink power allocation and user scheduling, maximizing sum ergodic throughput in an integrated LEO satellite and cell-free massive MIMO system (p. 3, 9-10).
system: LEO satellite with 5x5 antenna array (N=25), 40 single-antenna APs, single-antenna IoT users; no RIS; 3 GHz carrier, 20 MHz bandwidth (p. 3, 10).
method: Heterogeneous GNN (SHGNN) with MLP aggregation and combination, mean pooling, sigmoid power output; unsupervised training with negative-sum-rate loss on statistical CSI (p. 9-10).
data_channel: Simulated only: Rayleigh AP-user links, spatially correlated Rician satellite-user links, custom path-loss and shadowing formulas (shadowing variance cites [44]); no public dataset (p. 3, 10-11).
test_conditions: GNN-Stable trained with K=30 users and tested with K=20, 30, 40, 50; GNN-Robust trained and tested with the same K (p. 13).
baselines: Non-learned: AO Algorithm 1 (the paper's own), random and maximum-power allocation (Fig. 8, not compared with the GNN); learned: only GNN-Stable and GNN-Robust variants of SHGNN (p. 12-13).
metrics: Sum ergodic throughput (Mb/s), per-user throughput CDF, percentage of scheduled and unscheduled users, run time in ms (p. 11-13).
complexity: SHGNN complexity O(L(M+KN+KN^2)) (p. 10); run time 30-36 ms for GNN against 621-5089 ms for Algorithm 1, K=20 to 50 (Table I, p. 13).
q1_support: p. 3: "a Rician distribution, i.e.," - AP links follow Rayleigh fading and the satellite link a spatially correlated Rician model; path loss and shadowing formulas are written out on p. 10-11 (shadowing variance cites [44]) but no 3GPP model is stated and no measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "K = 30 users, while the testing phase is applied for a" - GNN-Stable is trained with K = 30 users and tested with K in {20, 30, 40, 50}, a different number of users than in training.
q3_support: p. 13: "Table I compares the performance of the learning-based" - and model-based approaches (SHGNN versus the non-learned Algorithm 1); the only learned comparators are GNN-Stable and GNN-Robust, two trainings of the same SHGNN, and no MLP, CNN or earlier learned power-control method is run.
q4_support: p. 10: "SHGNN is in order of O(L(M + KN + KN 2 ))" - complexity of the proposed GNN; Table I (p. 13) also gives run times in ms.
q5_support: p. 10: "We now evaluate the analysis and optimal power allocation" - evaluation on a simulated system of 40 APs; no code or data link, DOI or public dataset is given anywhere.
notes: Included as area 6: the learned SHGNN controls the uplink transmit power (and scheduling) of a LEO satellite plus cell-free AP link, which is physical layer in satellite links; combining is MRC and is not learned (p. 1, 6). The satellite has N=25 antennas, so the system check also passes. Table I (p. 13) was read from the page image because the text extraction lost its numbers. q1 is 0 because [44] (a 3GPP NTN overview) is cited only for the shadowing variance. q3 is 0 because GNN-Stable and GNN-Robust are variants of the proposed SHGNN, and Algorithm 1, random and maximum power are non-learned.
